ABOUT THE PROJECT

The product

A companion app for a smart projector.

Tools
Figma · AI tools
Team
3 students
Duration
2 months
Context
Academic studies

The challenge

Instructions alone could not make projector setup clear.

Users juggled a long manual, the projector and a remote, with no feedback along the way. We brought setup and everyday use into one guided app.

The audience

Home users aged 18–50 with varying technical confidence.

With basic English, who want to start watching quickly.

KEY DECISIONS

Three significant decisions.

01UX · Navigation

Bring progress and navigation together

Progress at the top and navigation at the bottom split attention around the main action.

We grouped progress and navigation at the bottom, keeping the center for the instruction.

02UX · Information architecture

Give everyday actions direct access

Returning users often need screen mirroring and calibration, but reaching them meant going through the full Quick Setup every time.

We added direct access from Home, alongside its five existing areas.

03UI · Information hierarchy

Make device health clear at a glance

Filled circles, inconsistent colors and constant explanations made device health hard to read.

We used progress rings and a consistent palette, with details available in pop-ups.

My contribution.

As a team of three, we defined the app’s content, features and visual direction.

  • Feature access. Added screen mirroring and calibration to Home, for returning users.
  • Screen design. Designed the remote control, and worked on the Quick Setup and device-health screens.
  • Controls and feedback. Designed the Home icons and the Atmosphere controls and states.

AI use

Working with AI

We used AI tools at two points in the process:

ChatGPT, to generate the graphics for the Quick Setup screens, and Figma Make, to explore design directions during brainstorming.

The final screens and interface decisions were designed in Figma.
